title: ERC20 transfer/transferFrom return values ignored: deposit() credits balances even if token transferFrom returns false; withdraw() debits balances/totalDeposits before a possibly-failing/false-returning transfer
description: Discovery: rescan class 1/cross-function consistency + integration correctness (token return values). Vault treats IERC20.transferFrom/transfer as bool-returning but never checks the return value. If a non-compliant or misbehaving token returns false without reverting, deposit() will still increment balances[msg.sender] and totalDeposits without actually receiving tokens (unbacked credits). withdraw() debits balances[msg.sender] and totalDeposits before calling transfer; if transfer returns false (or behaves unexpectedly), tokens may not be sent but ledger state is already debited, creating loss for users or desyncs.
root_cause: Return values from transferFrom/transfer are ignored; no validation that the token transfer actually succeeded.

harm.who: depositors and withdrawers interacting with non-compliant ERC20 tokens (or tokens that can return false)
harm.loses_what: unbacked credits created on deposit (others can be redeemed against them), or tokens debited from ledger but not received on withdraw
harm.magnitude: up to the affected amounts; can create ledger/token desync proportional to transferred amounts

exploit_trace: 1. Assume a token returns false on transferFrom without reverting.
2. Attacker or user calls deposit(X); code ignores false and credits balances[user]+=X, totalDeposits+=X.
3. The vault received 0 tokens but the ledger shows X credit; other users' tokens can later be redeemed against this unbacked credit.
4. Alternatively, withdraw() debits ledger before transfer; if transfer returns false, user loses their credit with no tokens received.

preconditions.text: interaction with an ERC20 that returns false on failure instead of reverting

postconditions.text: vault ledger credits exceed actual token balance (unbacked)

audit_trail.who_benefits: No one; causes incorrect accounting/state integrity

recommendation: Check return values (or use SafeERC20). In withdraw, consider effects of transfer failure and whether to roll back state safely.
